videos.title: This U.S. Aircraft Carrier Is Rearming for Possible Strikes on Iran | WSJ
videos.description:
American warships in the Middle East are preparing for an escalation in fighting in case President Trump opts for a fresh round of attacks against Iran in the coming weeks, according to U.S. officials familiar with the planning. 

During a rare visit to a U.S. aircraft carrier and guided-missile destroyer operating in the Arabian Sea, the Wall Street Journal observed flight operations, as well as a significant replenishment of munitions and supplies– including a large delivery of standoff land attack missiles and bunker-buster bombs designed to penetrate ground targets.

videos.title: Why California’s $33B Bullet Train Is Now a $231B Problem | WSJ
videos.description:
California’s high-speed rail project promised to connect Los Angeles and San Francisco with trains traveling up to 220 mph. Eighteen years after voters approved Proposition 1A, the ambitious transportation project lacks any finished track and faces an uncertain future. Costs are now projected to reach $126 billion with land acquisition and regulatory hurdles still putting America’s largest active infrastructure endeavor in jeopardy.

WSJ travels to construction sites, analyzes satellite images and reviews legal filings to explain what comes next for the multi-billion-dollar project.

videos.title: Trump Remade the GOP. How Do the Ultrarich Feel? | WSJ
videos.description:
GREENWICH, Conn.—This is a town that has been shorthand in political circles for one word: fundraising.

Democratic and Republican donors throw open the doors of their beautiful homes and hold parties where candidates for office mingle, drink wine, munch on appetizers and take questions from people they hope will fund their campaigns.

WSJ’s Annie Linskey traveled home to Greenwich to get a sense for what some of the town leaders—and donors—are thinking as we approach President Trump’s final midterms.
